claim_verdicts.evidence: navigations.md: "EF Core relationships are defined by foreign keys. Navigations are layered over foreign keys to provide a natural, object-oriented view for reading and manipulating relationships." one-to-many.md lists them as separate parts: "One or more foreign key properties on the dependent entity ... For example, `Post.BlogId`." and "Optionally, a reference navigation on the dependent entity referencing the principal entity. For example, `Post.Blog`." The sample dependent declares both `public int BlogId` and `public Blog Blog`.

one-to-many.md: "In the example above, configuration of the relationships starts with `HasMany` on the principal entity type (`Blog`) and then follows this with `WithOne`. As with all relationships, it is exactly equivalent to start with dependent entity type (`Post`) and use `HasOne` followed by `WithMany`." and "Neither of these options is better than the other; they both result in exactly the same configuration." Both samples chain `.HasForeignKey(e => e.BlogId)`.

one-to-many.md, anatomy of a one-to-many: "Optionally, a collection navigation on the principal entity ... For example, `Blog.Posts`." / "Optionally, a reference navigation on the dependent entity ... For example, `Post.Blog`." Same page: "Notice that the call to `WithOne` has no arguments. This is the way to tell EF that there is no navigation from `Post` to `Blog`." and "Notice again that `WithMany()` is called with no arguments to indicate that there is no navigation in this direction."

keys.md: "You can also configure multiple properties to be the key of an entity - this is known as a composite key. Conventions will only set up a composite key in specific cases - like for an owned type collection." The Fluent API sample it links, samples/core/Modeling/Keys/FluentAPI/KeyComposite.cs, is `modelBuilder.Entity<Car>().HasKey(c => new { c.State, c.LicensePlate });` — the same anonymous-type shape the lesson uses.

`git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs` (stage-1^{commit} = 4fca60a), lines 25-43: `Order` declares `Id`, `CustomerId` (int), `PlacedAt`, `Status`, `Items` (List<OrderItem>) and `Customer` (`Customer?`); `OrderItem` declares only `OrderId`, `ProductId`, `Quantity`, `UnitPriceVnd` — no `Id`. `tools/extract-code ... --lines 25-43` output is character-identical to the lesson's first code block.

`tools/extract-code DonHang.Infrastructure/DonHangDbContext.cs --tag stage-1 --lines 38-57` returns exactly the lesson's second code block, including `e.HasMany(o => o.Items).WithOne().HasForeignKey(i => i.OrderId);`, `e.HasOne(o => o.Customer).WithMany().HasForeignKey(o => o.CustomerId);` and `e.HasKey(i => new { i.OrderId, i.ProductId });`, indentation included.

Entities.cs @ stage-1, full file: `Customer` declares Id, FullName, Email, City, PasswordHash only — no collection of orders; `OrderItem` declares OrderId, ProductId, Quantity, UnitPriceVnd only — no reference back to `Order`. That matches the two no-argument calls `WithOne()` and `WithMany()` in DonHangDbContext.cs lines 45-46.

Live run this session against the running stage-1 lab (donhang-api, localhost:8080): POST /api/v1/auth/login with anh.tran@example.com / donhang-dev-password returned a token; GET /api/v1/orders with it returned `[{"id":1,"status":"paid","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"},{"id":2,"status":"shipped","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"},{"id":10,"status":"paid","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"}]`; the same call without a token returns 401. OrdersController.List builds `new OrderSummaryDto(o.Id, o.Status, o.Customer!.FullName)`.

navigations.md: "Reference navigations for required relationships can be nullable or non-nullable." one-to-many.md: "the reference navigation must be nullable if the foreign key property is nullable. If the foreign key property is non-nullable, then the reference navigation may be nullable or not." foreign-and-principal-keys.md: "the nullability of the foreign key property determines whether a relationship is optional or required. However, a nullable foreign key property can be used for a required relationship ... by calling IsRequired".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/efcore-docs .../relationships/navigations.md L28-33; one-to-many.md L63; foreign-and-principal-keys.md L80
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A reference navigation's nullability is a free choice only when the foreign key property is non-nullable; with C# nullable reference types it must be nullable if the FK property is nullable. Optional vs required is governed by the FK property (not the column), unless IsRequired/[Required] overrides it.

issues.quote: A primary key where `order_id` alone and `product_id` alone each match several rows, but the pair matches exactly one
issues.text: The marked-correct option states something false of this system's own data and of composite keys in general. In db/seed.sql, order 2 has exactly one item — `(2, 3, 1, 890000)` — so `order_id = 2` alone matches exactly one row; orders 4, 6, 9 and 11 are the same. A composite key is about which values are *guaranteed* unique, not about how many rows one part happens to match. The key stays (a) — b, c, d are clearly wrong — but as worded (a) teaches a rule the reader can falsify with the lesson's own data.
issues.fix: Reword option a to the guarantee: "A primary key where neither `order_id` nor `product_id` alone is guaranteed to identify one row — only the two together always do" (vi: "Một khóa chính mà riêng `order_id` hay riêng `product_id` đều không đảm bảo định danh đúng một dòng — chỉ cặp cả hai mới luôn làm được"), and drop "matches every item of one order" from the explanation in favour of the same wording.
